subject: Science
title: Food from plants and animals
objectives: Children will say which foods come from plants and which from animals.
Children will name foods that help them grow.
content: Foods that come from plants, foods that come from animals, and healthy foods that help us grow.
teachingActivities: Use real foods or large pictures; sort into two groups; speak positively about all foods; check family diets and allergies; link to the market and the kitchen.
learnerActivities: Sort foods into those from plants and those from animals and name healthy foods.
resources: Pictures or toy foods: yam, rice, beans, tomato, egg, milk, fish, meat
Plate pictures of a healthy meal
assessment: Observe whether each child names two plant foods and two animal foods and says healthy food helps us grow.
expectedOutcomes: Names two plant foods and two animal foods.
Says that healthy food helps us grow.

lessons.title: Foods from plants
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name foods that come from plants.
successCriteria: Names at least three plant foods
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name fruits and know that plants grow from seeds.
resources: Toy or real yam, rice, beans and tomato
lessons.starter: Hold up a yam and say "A yam grows in the ground. It comes from a plant."
teacherActivities: Show each food and name it.
Say "Yams grow under the soil. Tomatoes grow on plants."
Ask "Which food comes from a plant?"
Let each child pick a food and say where it grows.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children listen and point to the pictures.
Child points to a plant food.
Child shows the food and says a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each food and name it. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Yams grow under the soil. Tomatoes grow on plants." Children: Children listen and point to the pictures.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Which food comes from a plant?" Children: Child points to a plant food.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick a food and say where it grows. Children: Child shows the food and says a word.

practical.title: Plant foods
steps: Put plant foods on a tray.
Each child picks one and names it.
practical.safety: If real foods are used, wash them and check allergies. Keep food for looking unless tasting is planned and cleared.

differentiation.support: Offer two foods and say the name first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name a plant food they eat at home.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Does rice come from a plant?

lessons.conclusion: Put the foods in the basket and say "Thank you, plants."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about plant foods when you cook, such as yam and beans.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name foods that come from plants" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Foods from animals
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name foods that come from animals.
successCriteria: Names at least three animal foods
Says which animal gives each food
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name fruits and know that plants grow from seeds.
resources: Pictures or toys of an egg, milk, fish and meat
Animal pictures: hen, cow, fish, goat
lessons.starter: Show an egg and say "An egg comes from a hen." Show milk and say "Milk comes from a cow."
teacherActivities: Show each food and the animal it comes from.
Say a food and ask "Which animal gives us this?"
Match the foods to the animals.
Talk about how animals give us food and need our care.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Child points to the animal.
Child places the food next to its animal.
Children listen and nod.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each food and the animal it comes from. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say a food and ask "Which animal gives us this?" Children: Child points to the animal.
Step 3. Teacher: Match the foods to the animals. Children: Child places the food next to its animal.
Step 4. Teacher: Talk about how animals give us food and need our care. Children: Children listen and nod.

practical.title: Animal foods
steps: Put foods and animal pictures on the mat.
practical.safety: Use pictures or toy foods and be sensitive to families who do not eat certain foods. Check allergies before any tasting.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and say the food first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say which animal gives us eggs.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cards away and say "Thank you, animals."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about foods from animals at mealtimes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name foods that come from animals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Plant or animal food?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sort foods into plant foods and animal foods.
successCriteria: Sorts a food into the right basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name fruits and know that plants grow from seeds.
resources: Two baskets labelled plant and animal
lessons.starter: Show two baskets and say "One is for foods from plants. One is for foods from animals."
teacherActivities: Pick up a rice picture and put it in the plant basket.
Pick up an egg picture and put it in the animal basket.
Let each child pick a picture and choose a basket.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say plant.
Children watch and say animal.
Child sorts the picture.
Children name the foods.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick up a rice picture and put it in the plant basket. Children: Children watch and say plant.
Step 2. Teacher: Pick up an egg picture and put it in the animal basket. Children: Children watch and say animal.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick a picture and choose a basket. Children: Child sorts the picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each basket together. Children: Children name the foods.

practical.title: Food sort
steps: Put two baskets on the mat.
Each child picks a food picture.
Put it in the plant or animal basket.
practical.safety: Use large pictures. Keep the floor clear and supervise turns.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and say where the food comes from.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another food for each basket.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is egg a plant food?
questions.expected: No, it is from an animal.

expectedOutcomes: Sorts foods into plant and animal
Says plant or animal with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the pictures away and say "Plants and animals give us food."
lessons.homeConnection: Sort foods in the kitchen into plant and animal foods.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort foods into plant foods and animal foods" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Healthy food helps me grow
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name healthy foods and say they help us grow.
successCriteria: Says that healthy food helps us grow
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name fruits and know that plants grow from seeds.
resources: Pictures of fruit, vegetables, beans, rice, fish and water
lessons.starter: Show a plate with healthy foods and say "These foods help us grow strong."
teacherActivities: Show each healthy food and say its name.
Say "We eat these to grow tall and strong." Stretch up tall.
Show foods that we only have sometimes, such as sweets.
Let each child choose foods for a healthy plate.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children stretch up and say strong.
Children listen and nod.
Child puts pictures on a plate.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each healthy food and say its name. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "We eat these to grow tall and strong." Stretch up tall. Children: Children stretch up and say strong.
Step 3. Teacher: Show foods that we only have sometimes, such as sweets. Children: Children listen and nod.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose foods for a healthy plate. Children: Child puts pictures on a plate.

practical.title: Healthy plate
steps: Put food pictures on the mat.
Each child picks foods for a plate.
practical.safety: Be sensitive to family circumstances and food availability. Focus on foods children know and never shame any child.

differentiation.support: Offer two foods and choose the healthy one together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what they eat to grow strong.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says healthy food helps us grow
lessons.conclusion: Stretch up tall and say "I will grow strong."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about healthy foods at mealtimes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name healthy foods and say they help us grow" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 food check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names and sorts foods.
successCriteria: Names two plant foods and two animal foods
Says that healthy food helps us grow
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name fruits and know that plants grow from seeds.
lessons.starter: Sing the food song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: plant foods, animal foods and the healthy plate.
At each station ask "What is this food?" and "Where does it come from?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or gesture.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: plant foods, animal foods and the healthy plate. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this food?" and "Where does it come from?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Food stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use pictures or toy foods.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two foods.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend about healthy food.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names plant foods; names animal foods; sorts foods; says healthy food helps us grow.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
Sorts foods and names healthy foods
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the food pictures.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about food sources at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names and sorts foods" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
